newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up sharply with gas, spot power.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up sharply with gas, spot power.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended sharply higher Wednesday, taking strength from higher priced natural gas and strong Western spot electricity prices, industry sources said.
Talk of a storm expected to hit the U.S. Northwest over the next few days also helped buoy electricity futures, sources said, although forecasts were not calling for much-below normal temperatures.
West Coast spot power rose in value Wednesday, with players looking for higher demand as a result of the storm.
NYMEX Henry Hub January electricity futures also closed higher on the day.

January California Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures closed up $1.97 at $26.97 after hitting a new contact high of $27.20, while February COB ended up $1.25 at $20.85 after trade as high as $21.20 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds finished up between 30 and 75 cents, with March, July, October, November and December all hitting new contract highs.
COB volume was strong for the contract, with an estimated total of 934 lots traded, surpassing March 29 opening day volume for the contract of 923 lots, NYMEX said.
January Palo Verde (PV) settled up $2.20 at $26.83 after hitting a new contract high of $27.50, while February finished up $1.50 at $21.75 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds finished 15 cents at $1.00 higher.
Palo Verde traded an estimated 244 contracts Wednesday, NYMEX said.
